counterfactual_missing_items: No epidermal atypia to suggest an epidermal-derived neoplasm
No findings of prominent atypical or malignant intralobular cells to support angiosarcoma
No symptoms from chronic venous insufficiency or port-wine stains
decisive_items: KDR (VEGFR2) c.C2312G, p.T771R identified as the only somatic mutation
Discrete clusters of small-caliber vessels were observed, with superficial, small lobules of small-caliber vessels.
Histopathologic analysis of affected tissue and blood
response.rationale: R2 precisely integrates the clinical appearance of a discrete telangiectatic plaque, the distinct vascular histology, and the confirmed somatic KDR mutation. The other options describe variants of this clinical/pathological/genetic picture less precisely: R6 gives only a descriptive morphology; R5 requires keratotic epidermal features absent here; R1 and R4 imply different morphological malformation and maybe angiosarcomatous changes, not described; R3 similarly is a non-tumor description.

rejected.why: A description of a morphological malformation, not a diagnosis; it lacks the genetic and histologic specificity of the lesion.
Confusing an angiokeratoma, which in this lesion does not have the hyperkeratotic and clinical/angiographic characteristics needed.
Angiosarcoma is characterized by infiltrating atypical endothelial proliferation, not a regular discrete dermal cluster of benign vascular channels.
Telangiectasia is a symptom that reflects the appearance of a vascular lesion, but the presence of the only KDR mutation and histological pattern suggest a clonal/somatic vascular cause.
